content.question: Which statement about morphology is correct?
options: Inflectional morphology creates new dictionary words, while derivational morphology only changes grammatical form.
Inflectional morphology changes grammatical form (e.g., walk -> walked) without creating a new word, while derivational morphology creates new words (e.g., happy -> unhappiness).
Both inflectional and derivational morphology only affect pronunciation, never meaning.
Morphemes are always whole words that cannot be decomposed further.
content.answer: Inflectional morphology changes grammatical form (e.g., walk -> walked) without creating a new word, while derivational morphology creates new words (e.g., happy -> unhappiness).
